# AGENTS.md

Guidance for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, …) working in this repository. This is the single source of truth: `.claude/CLAUDE.md` only imports it. Edit this file, not that one.

## Project

"aipocalypse" — a PC first-person shooter built in Unity **6000.6.7f1** (Unity 6) with URP 17.6. Development happens in the Unity Editor; the `*.csproj`/`*.slnx` files at the repo root are generated by Unity — never edit them.

**Editor control: Unity CLI** (`unity`, via the `com.unity.pipeline` package). The deprecated Unity MCP is not used. The CLI's docs ship with the package in `Library/PackageCache/com.unity.pipeline@*/Documentation~/` (`commands/`, `authoring-commands.md`, `testing.md`, …); in Claude Code, also load the official `unity:unity-cli` skill. Read them before editor work.

- Use `unity command <name>` to drive the live editor (scenes, GameObjects, components, prefabs, assets, captures, console) instead of hand-editing `.unity`/`.prefab`/`.asset` YAML. `unity command` lists the command groups (`unity command <group>` lists a group); follow the package docs (`script recompile` → `script recompile_status` → `test run` loop, `script run` for bulk/plugin work, `script eval` for one-liners). Older docs and skills may use the pre-rename flat names (`run_script`, `run_tests`, `set_autotick`); the CLI error names the replacement.
- In Git Bash pass `--project-path "$(cygpath -w "$PWD")"` — the CLI doesn't match `/d/...` paths.
- Before editor work run `unity status` and `unity command editor set_auto_tick --enable true` (commands stall while Unity is unfocused otherwise); if not ready, check Safe Mode (`unity pipeline list`) or ask the user to open the project.
- Verify changes with `script recompile_status` / `console status` + `console get` / `capture scene_view` instead of guessing. Tests use `com.unity.test-framework` (`unity command test run --mode editor`).
- Only one agent drives the editor at a time. When two agents work in parallel, use separate branches/worktrees.

## Skills

Skills live in **`.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md`** (Codex reads this path; `.claude/skills` is a symlink to it — needs `git config core.symlinks true` and Windows Developer Mode on each clone). **Before working in an area below, read the matching `SKILL.md`** (and its `references/` when it points there). They are checked against the installed package sources; where a skill conflicts with this file or `docs/technicals/`, the project docs win.

| Skill | Read before |
| --- | --- |
| `aipocalypse-architecture` | Registrations, scopes, installers, injection; gameplay events (MessagePipe); any async/await, delays, pause; C# touching serialization, statics, play-mode hooks, build defines or Unity 6.6 APIs |
| `aipocalypse-enemy-ai` | Any enemy/companion/NPC movement or AI decision: EnemySystem, Behavior Designer Pro trees ticked by `EnemyManager`, A* `FollowerEntity`, navmesh, spawning |
| `tools-unity-feel` | Game feel / feedbacks (allowed vs banned feedbacks; points to Feel's own skills) |
| `tools-unity-broaudio` | Any sound, music or ambience: `AudioService`, `SoundID`s, BroAudio libraries (points to BroAudio's `CLAUDE.md`) |
| `tools-unity-audio-tools` | Editing audio clips in the editor: trim, normalize, fade, export (points to Audio Tools' own skills) |
| `tools-unity-text-studio` | Animated / typewriter text (Text Studio is Undecided: ask first; points to its own skills) |
| `tools-unity-map-generation` | Building or changing a map: layout from a concept, generated heights/water/vegetation/boundary/dressing, rebuilds, map art packs and perf, and how MicroVerse is used here (the WorldMap generator; step runner and MicroVerse kit in `scripts/`) |
| `tools-unity-stylized-water` | Any Stylized Water 3 work: water bodies, RiverModeler rivers, waterfalls, underwater, height queries, water materials and perf |

The project skills hold only what is specific to this repo. Library detail lives in generic user-scope skills in Claude Code (`~/.claude/skills/`): `unity-vcontainer`, `unity-messagepipe`, `unity-unitask`, `unity-6-new-apis`, `unity-behavior-designer-pro`, `unity-astar`, `unity-microverse`, and `unity-optimization-pc` for measuring or optimising performance. The project skills point to them; when they are not available (other agents, other machines), read the package source under `Packages/` or `Library/PackageCache/` instead of guessing.

To add a skill: create `.agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter, and add a row here. The `tools-unity-*` skills started from [tjboudreaux/cc-plugin-unity-gamedev](https://github.com/tjboudreaux/cc-plugin-unity-gamedev) (MIT, `.agents/skills/THIRD_PARTY_LICENSE-unity-gamedev.txt`).

## Where things live

- `Assets/_Game/` — **all first-party game code and content go here.** Stable mechanics live in `Assets/_Game/_Core/` (one folder per system plus `_Bootstrap`, `_Common`, `_Debug`); design-dependent rules will go in `Assets/_Game/Features/` and trial mechanics in `Assets/_Game/_Experimental/`, both created with their first code (only the `Aipocalypse.Core` and two test asmdefs exist today). Features depend on Core, never the reverse; their asmdefs will enforce it once they exist. Content lives in one folder per thing (`Assets/_Game/Content/<Kind>/<Name>/`: `Enemies`, `Items` and `Weapons` exist; other kinds such as animals or companions get a folder when the first one is added); system-wide settings ScriptableObjects in `Assets/_Game/Data/<System>/`; maps in `Assets/_Game/Maps/<Map>/` with the shared environment kit in `Assets/_Game/Environment/`. Full layout and rules and system ownership: `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`; script map: `docs/technicals/CODE_STRUCTURE.md`.
- `Assets/_Game/Scenes/Prototypes/` — `WorldMap.unity`, the prototype world map, not in Build Settings. Mechanics are currently tested there; `Proto_*` scenes that test one mechanic each are planned. Prototype scenes use the real code and prefabs, never copies (rules in ARCHITECTURE.md → "Prototypes → main game").
- `Assets/_StoreAssets/` and `Assets/Synty/` — third-party art/asset-store content (Synty packs, Low Poly Weapon Bundles 1–3, Stylized Grass/Water 3, Damage Numbers Pro, Feel…). Treat as vendor code: don't modify; reference or make variants/prefabs under `_Game`. Full inventory: `docs/technicals/PLUGINS.md`.
- `Assets/_Placeholder/` — temporary/placeholder assets (e.g. borrowed audio) waiting for final replacements. Fine to reference from `_Game`, but nothing here is meant to ship.
- `Assets/Plugins/` — third-party editor/runtime tooling (Odin Inspector, DOTween/Demigiant, GPUInstancerPro, etc.). Don't modify.
- `Assets/_Game/Settings/` — URP assets (`PC_RPAsset`, `PC_Renderer`), volume profile, and Input System config. `Assets/Settings/` holds the Build Profiles and an unused URP global settings asset (the live one is in `_Game/Settings`).
- Build Settings list no scenes yet. What only one map uses lives in `Assets/_Game/Maps/<Map>/` (WorldMap's terrain, water meshes, navmesh and backdrop are in `Maps/WorldMap/`, its scene in `Scenes/Prototypes/`). When a map becomes official, its scene goes to `Maps/<Map>/<Map>.unity` and into Build Settings.
- `Packages/` — local packages: A* Pathfinding Project (`com.arongranberg.astar`), GPU Instancer Pro (`com.gurbu.gpui-pro` + modules), Behavior Designer Pro (`com.opsive.*`), COZY, MicroVerse, Spline Spawner, SC Screen Effects (`xyz.staggart-creations.screen-effects`).
- `AgentScripts/` — editor scripts outside `Assets/`, run with `unity command run_script` (the map generator in `AgentScripts/Maps/<Map>/`, setup, review and perf scripts per feature). `Tools/` holds the same kind of one-off editor script (e.g. `HandFistReview.cs`).

## Key tech choices (from `Packages/manifest.json`)

- **Input**: new Input System only (`activeInputHandler: 1`). Actions asset is `Assets/_Game/Settings/InputSystem_Actions.inputactions` with a `Player` map: Move, Look, Attack, Interact, Crouch, Jump, Previous, Next, Sprint, Slot1–Slot9, Drop, Aim, Reload; and a `Debug` map (editor and dev builds only): NextHour (N), NextPhase (M), KillPlayer (K), RevivePlayer (L). Use these actions; don't call the legacy `UnityEngine.Input`. Game code reads input only through `InputService` (root scope, generated wrapper `GameInputActions`); never enable/disable actions or set the cursor lock elsewhere.
- **Architecture / DI**: VContainer (`jp.hadashikick.vcontainer`) + UniTask. Cross-system events go through MessagePipe. No `X.Instance` singletons in game code — services are plain C# registered in lifetime scopes; each system registers through its own installer. Entity prefabs (player, enemies…) carry their own `EntityScope` and must work dropped into any scene. See `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`.
- **AI**: Behavior Designer Pro 3.3 trees for every agent; crowd enemy trees ticked time-sliced by `EnemyManager`.
- **Enemy navigation**: A* Pathfinding Project 5.4 (`FollowerEntity` agents).
- **Camera**: Cinemachine 6.6 (Cinemachine 3 API, namespace `Unity.Cinemachine`).
- **Rendering/perf**: URP, GPU Instancer Pro for foliage/props, VFX Graph, Splines, Terrain Tools.
- **Editor conveniences**: Odin Inspector (`Sirenix`), DOTween, Feel (MoreMountains), Damage Numbers Pro are available for game code.

## Plugins — check before building, use them correctly

Many runtime and editor plugins are installed (Feel, BroAudio, Easy Save 3, Damage Numbers Pro, DOTween, Odin, GPU Instancer Pro, A*, Behavior Designer Pro, Localization…). **Read `docs/technicals/PLUGINS.md` before any task that a plugin might cover.**

- **Check first:** before writing a system or tool, check whether an installed plugin already does it. Use the plugin rather than reinventing it, unless PLUGINS.md says otherwise.
- **Use it the documented way:** follow the plugin's rules in PLUGINS.md (e.g. no plugin singletons/static event systems in gameplay code, `TimeService` owns `Time.timeScale`, uGUI for UI, DOTween for code tweens, behavior trees for all AI with crowd trees ticked by `EnemyManager`). When unsure how a plugin works, read its docs or source in `Assets/Plugins/` / `Packages/` instead of guessing (some ship their own guide, e.g. `Assets/Plugins/BroAudio/CLAUDE.md`).
- **Use it efficiently:** prefer the plugin's pooling, batching and caching features (Damage Numbers Pro and BroAudio pooling, GPUI instancing) and keep per-instance plugin components off crowd entities (exceptions: BD `BehaviorTree` in Manual mode, A* `FollowerEntity`).
- **Keep PLUGINS.md current:** when adding, removing or starting to use a plugin in a new way, update it in the same change.

## Prompt first, GDD second

When writing code, the user's prompt is the spec.

- Build what the prompt asks. Don't add mechanics, rules or numbers the prompt didn't ask for.
- You may read `docs/gdd/` for context, but anything taken from it (a rule, a mechanic, a number, a constraint) must be **proposed and confirmed by the user before you implement it**. Say what it is and where it comes from (e.g. "CORE.md says stamina drains when sprinting — add it?").
- If the prompt and the GDD disagree, follow the prompt and mention the difference; don't "fix" the code toward the GDD.
- Technical docs (`docs/technicals/`, this file) still decide *how* to build.

## Keeping docs current

- When you add or change a core system (data structures, gameplay flow, system boundaries), update the relevant section of this file or `docs/` in the same change. Keep this file high-level; put detail in `docs/`.
- `docs/gdd/` — game design. Design intent: `docs/gdd/GDD.md` is the index of per-topic files; start with `docs/gdd/CORE.md` (pitch, pillars, core loop). `docs/gdd/IDEAS.md` is a draft scratchpad, not canon — never implement from it unless explicitly asked.
- `docs/technicals/` — technical docs. Architecture and data flow: `docs/technicals/ARCHITECTURE.md`. Script map (what each script owns, dependencies, frame order): `docs/technicals/CODE_STRUCTURE.md` — update it whenever you add, move or remove a script. Plugin inventory and usage rules: `docs/technicals/PLUGINS.md`. UI (HUD canvas, widgets, styles, adding info): `docs/technicals/UI.md`. Equipment (items, hotbar, switching, belt lantern, adding item kinds): `docs/technicals/EQUIPMENT.md`. Weapons (guns, ammo, bullets, recoil, melee, adding a weapon): `docs/technicals/WEAPONS.md`. First-person hands (grips, hand poses, weapon clip authoring, swapping the hand mesh): `docs/technicals/HANDS.md`. World map environment (terrain generator, water, vegetation, atmosphere, rebuild order): `docs/technicals/ENVIRONMENT.md`. Day/night cycle (world clock, time-of-day looks, sky, reactors, player light at night, ambience, HUD clock): `docs/technicals/DAYNIGHT.md`.
- Current milestone/tasks: `docs/ROADMAP.md`.

## Code style

Base convention: the `oss-unity:csharp-unity` skill (Claude Code; other agents read `~/.claude/oss-skills/oss-unity/skills/csharp-unity/SKILL.md`). Read it before writing C#: early returns, one responsibility per class, cached lookups, GC-free hot paths, lifecycle and Unity 6 API rules. Its own house style yields to this file; **where they disagree, this section wins**:

- **Naming:** PascalCase types, methods, properties, public fields, consts and `static readonly`; `_camelCase` for every private field, serialized or not; camelCase locals and parameters; `I` prefix on interfaces; `Async` suffix on UniTask methods. No `m_` / `k_` / `s_` prefixes.
- Leave out `private` (it's the default) and don't write `this.`. Mark leaf classes `sealed`. No `#region`.
- **Serialized fields:** always `[SerializeField] T _field;` with a read-only property when other code needs it (`public T Field => _field;`). **Never `[field: SerializeField]` auto-properties**: their serialized name `<Field>k__BackingField` breaks on a rename and can't be found with `FindProperty("_field")`. Public fields only in nested `[Serializable]` data structs/classes. When renaming a serialized field, add `[FormerlySerializedAs("oldName")]` (or migrate the assets and drop it).
- Block-scoped namespaces matching the folder (CODE_STRUCTURE.md), `using` lines outside the namespace, braces on their own line; a single-statement `if`/loop body may drop its braces. `var` when the type is obvious.
- A `Tooltip` instead of a comment on serialized fields whose meaning or units aren't obvious.
- Async, cancellation, events and lookups follow `aipocalypse-architecture` (MessagePipe across systems, VContainer instead of `Find*`, no `destroyCancellationToken` on pooled objects), not the skill's generic advice.
- No XML/docstring blocks. At most one short `//` line on a method to state its purpose; skip it when the name is self-explanatory.
- Don't add comments narrating a fix or adjustment ("changed X to Y", "fixed bug"). Comment only for important/critical fixes, workarounds, or non-obvious solutions, and explain the *why*.
- Serialized key→value data uses Unity 6.6's built-in `[SerializeField] Dictionary<TKey, TValue>` ([manual](https://docs.unity3d.com/6000.6/Documentation/Manual/script-serialization-dictionaries.html)), not a list of key/value structs or a custom `SerializableDictionary`. **Never use Odin serialization** (`SerializedMonoBehaviour`, `SerializedScriptableObject`, `[OdinSerialize]`, Odin serialized collections) in any case; Odin is for inspector attributes only.

## Conventions / gotchas

- Commit messages in history use the style `+ add <thing>` (e.g. `+ add synty prototype`).
- `.gitattributes` is the standard Unity template with Git LFS for binary asset types; make sure LFS is installed before committing/pulling large assets.
- Always commit `.meta` files together with their assets; never delete/rename asset files outside the Unity Editor (or move the `.meta` alongside) or GUID references break.
- Main branch is `develop`.
- Never name git branches in skills or docs (branches get deleted); describe the change or point at files on `develop`.
